brief.headline: Memory Rally Extends; CoWoS Gap Narrows; Hyperscaler Capex Hits $775B
brief.summary: <cite index="11-3,13-7">DDR4 8Gb PC DRAM hit $24 in July, up 14.3% MoM, marking the highest level since tracking began in June 2016</cite>. <cite index="13-1">NAND flash (128Gb 16Gx8 MLC) reached $30.1, up 4.3% MoM</cite>, with <cite index="17-1,17-2">TrendForce projecting Q3 DRAM contract prices up 13-18% QoQ and NAND up 10-15%</cite>. <cite index="20-2,20-6">US hyperscalers committed $660-690B capex for 2026, nearly doubling 2025 levels, with the vast majority directed at AI compute and data centers</cite>. <cite index="30-10">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is expected to narrow from ~20% currently to ~10% by end-2026</cite>, though <cite index="5-3">SK Hynix will likely hold ~50% HBM market share in 2026</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, versus Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%</cite>. <cite index="42-9,42-10">SK Hynix increased DRAM pricing ~30% QoQ and NAND mid-50%, while Samsung raised DRAM 40%+ and NAND high-60%</cite>, but <cite index="42-4,42-5">peak earnings might be lower than anticipated, evidenced by pricing weakness relative to expectations over the last three months</cite>. Long SK Hynix / short Samsung on HBM qualification lead and market share stability, though both face valuation risk after YTD gains of <cite index="6-1,6-4">114% (Samsung) and 186% (SK Hynix)</cite>. Samsung's persistent HBM3E qual delays vs. Nvidia remain the asymmetric risk.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="8-1,8-10">Manufacturers are diverting production lines towards HBM stacks and enterprise-grade DDR5, squeezing supply of flash and mobile memory</cite>. <cite index="8-4">Top three memory makers have already allocated their full HBM output for the year, with Micron guiding for 68% gross margin in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected to last through 2027, giving leading suppliers stronger pricing power than the industry has historically enjoyed</cite>. Structural demand from AI offsetting consumer weakness, but <cite index="6-9,6-10">TurboQuant release caused sharp decline in memory provider share prices, though structural shift remains to be seen</cite>. Watch for peak earnings risk in H2.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-1,5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B gigabits, with TSMC's latest call showing AI demand running well ahead of earlier forecasts</cite>. <cite index="5-7">SK Hynix expects only minimal to modest HBM3E price downtick for 2026 vs 2025 as more suppliers come online</cite>. <cite index="1-5">Micron announced integration of its HBM3E 36GB 12-high offering into AMD Instinct MI350 Series</cite>. <cite index="5-4">Nvidia negotiating with SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron on HBM3E pricing, with possible pushback as Samsung inches closer to qualification</cite>. Samsung's qual status remains the key binary for H2 share dynamics.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 PC DRAM hits $24 in July, up 14.3% MoM, record high since June 2016
news_pulse.implication: Sustained AI-driven capacity reallocation pushing conventional DRAM to multi-year highs; PC OEM cost pressure rising into H2.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce: Q3 DRAM contract +13-18% QoQ, NAND +10-15% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Pricing momentum decelerating but still double-digit; consumer demand softening while enterprise remains tight.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers commit $660-690B capex for 2026, nearly doubling 2025
news_pulse.implication: Unprecedented infrastructure spend sustains HBM/server DRAM demand, but $600B revenue gap vs capex raising ROI concerns.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply gap to narrow from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging bottleneck easing faster than expected; capacity reaching 115-140K wpm by end-2026.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix to hold ~50% HBM market share in 2026 - UBS
news_pulse.implication: Market share stability despite Samsung qual progress; Hynix positioned to defend leadership through 2026.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix -9.7%, Samsung -6.1% on Aug 6 Asia tech selloff
news_pulse.implication: Violent sector rotation amplified by leveraged chip bets in KOSPI; AI sentiment now bellwether for Korea volatility.

news_pulse.headline: Memory pricing below analyst expectations despite +30-40% DRAM, +50-60% NAND QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Peak earnings risk surfacing; pricing gains strong but missing Street forecasts, suggesting cycle topping dynamics.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung & SK Hynix sign OpenAI LoI for 900K DRAM wafers/month for Stargate
news_pulse.implication: Long-term capacity locked by hyperscalers; Samsung P5 (2028) and SK Hynix M15X (mid-2027) critical for 2027+ supply.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="40-2,40-9">Aug 6 selloff saw SK Hynix -9.71% and Samsung -6.13%</cite>, reflecting heightened vol in AI-linked semis post-US tech pullback. <cite index="6-1,6-4">YTD gains of 186% (SK Hynix) and 114% (Samsung)</cite> have stretched valuations to single-digit P/E multiples on peak earnings expectations. KOSPI program buying halted intraday on Aug 6, signaling exchange circuit-breaker risk. Watch ADR-KRX basis and vol surface for next rotation trigger.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung HBM3E Nvidia qual update or denial
Any hyperscaler capex guidance revision (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL earnings flow)
KOSPI intraday vol >3% indicating program buying/selling halts
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot price revision for Aug
TSMC CoWoS allocation updates for Nvidia Rubin vs. AMD MI400
